title: Winning for the Wrong Reason in Small Caps | Dimensional
gist: In the year to June 30, 2026, US small cap leadership came from exactly the stocks Dimensional classifies as lower expected return — low profitability growth and high asset growth names — so the 10 largest active US small cap funds' one-year returns rose with their weight in those stocks (top tercile: 14.8% weight, 43.1% return; bottom tercile: 4.4% weight, 33.1% return). Wes Crill's point is an attribution warning, not a market call: a 10-percentage-point performance gap was manufactured by holding the historically worst-performing cohort, so short-term small cap manager rankings currently reward the wrong exposure.

themes.theme: The junk cohort led small caps to June 2026

insights.claim: Over the year ending June 30, 2026, the biggest winners in US small caps were low profitability and high asset growth stocks — the two cohorts Dimensional systematically excludes as having lower expected returns.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Any small cap sleeve that outperformed over this window should be attributed before being rewarded — the alpha may just be junk beta that mean-reverts.
insights.quote: Over the past year, the big winners in US small caps happened to have been low profitability and high asset growth stocks.
insights.locator: Over the past year, the big winners

insights.claim: Among the 10 largest active US small cap funds, one-year returns to June 30, 2026 rose monotonically with allocation to lower expected return stocks: the top tercile by weight held 14.8% versus 4.4% for the bottom tercile, and returned 43.1% versus 33.1%.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
entities: active US small cap equity funds
insights.so_what: A 10-percentage-point manager dispersion was explained by a ~10-point holdings difference in one factor cohort — screen small cap manager shortlists on this exposure before hiring on trailing one-year numbers.
insights.quote: The average return for the top tercile was 43.1%, compared to just 33.1% for the bottom tercile.

insights.claim: Even the least junk-exposed large active US small cap funds returned roughly 33% over the twelve months to June 30, 2026, indicating a broad and very strong US small cap rally over that period, not just a narrow low-quality squeeze.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
entities: active US small cap equity funds
insights.so_what: After a ~33–43% one-year run in small caps, the base rate for forward returns and for the persistence of low-quality leadership both argue for trimming rather than chasing.

insights.claim: Dimensional argues that episodes in which lower-expected-return small caps outperform are transient, so the current leadership of low profitability and high asset growth names should not be extrapolated.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Positions the firm to keep its exclusion screens through the drawdown in relative performance; a reversal restores the screen's edge and punishes funds that drifted into the junk cohort.
insights.quote: While these periods of outperformance tend not to last, they can make it difficult to evaluate small cap manager relative performance.
insights.locator: However, sometimes the script gets flipped

insights.claim: Short-horizon manager evaluation can invert the signal: a manager can post top-quartile returns precisely because they held the stocks with the worst long-run expected returns, so the trailing number measures exposure luck rather than skill.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
entities: active US small cap equity funds
insights.so_what: Reusable due-diligence test: decompose any manager's outperformance into factor-cohort weights before allocating; reward process, not the tercile of the cohort that happened to run.
insights.quote: This illustrates one of the challenges with short-term performance: Sometimes managers win for the wrong reasons.
insights.locator: In other words, a larger allocation

insights.claim: Sorting a peer group by weight in a single lower-expected-return cohort — rather than by returns — is a practical diagnostic that reveals whether a category's recent performance dispersion is factor-driven.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
entities: active US small cap equity funds
insights.so_what: Cheap, repeatable screen: run holdings-weight terciles on any category where recent winners look anomalous, and treat monotone return-vs-weight patterns as evidence against skill.

insights.claim: Because the pattern holds across the 10 largest funds in the category, the junk-exposure tailwind affected the most widely owned US small cap vehicles rather than a fringe of small managers.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
entities: active US small cap equity funds
insights.so_what: Large allocator flows chasing one-year small cap league tables are, in aggregate, buying the low-profitability/high-asset-growth cohort at the top of its run.

themes.theme: Long-run cost of the excluded cohorts

insights.claim: From January 1975 to June 2026, US small cap growth low profitability stocks lagged the broader small cap space by more than eight percentage points and high asset growth small caps trailed by more than 12 percentage points, per Dimensional index comparisons.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President

insights.so_what: Sets the size of the prize: excluding these cohorts is worth roughly 8–12 points of relative return over a half-century, which dwarfs a single 10-point year of adverse dispersion.

insights.claim: Asset growth is presented as the stronger negative screen in US small caps than low profitability combined with high relative price, with a >12 point drag versus >8 points.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: If forced to run one exclusion in a small cap mandate, the balance-sheet-expansion screen historically did more work than the profitability/valuation screen.

insights.claim: Dimensional's small cap universe is defined as US NYSE/AMEX/Nasdaq companies in the lowest 8% of total eligible market capitalization, excluding non-US companies, REITs, UITs, and investment companies.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: The REIT and non-operating-company exclusions mean Dimensional small cap results are not directly comparable to Russell-style small cap benchmarks.

themes.theme: Index construction as an evolving screen

insights.claim: The Dimensional US Small Cap Index only added profitability as an inclusion factor in January 2014 and asset growth in December 2019, meaning its pre-2014 and pre-2019 track record is backtested under a different, less selective rule set.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Discount the 1975–2026 relative-return figures for in-sample construction: the screens were codified after the periods in which they are shown to have worked.
insights.quote: The calculation methodology for the index was amended in January 2014 to include profitability as a factor in selecting securities for inclusion in the index.

insights.claim: The Dimensional US Small High Asset Growth Index was only created in December 2019 and the Small Growth Low Profitability Index in February 2016, so the entire 1975-onward comparison series for both is retrospectively calculated rather than live.

insights.claim: Dimensional defines its lower-expected-return small cap cohort as the intersection of lowest profitability and highest relative price, not low profitability alone — a joint screen rather than a simple quality filter.

insights.so_what: Replicating the screen requires conditioning profitability on valuation; cheap unprofitable small caps are not the cohort being excluded.
